audit.summary: No critical or high severity vulnerabilities found. Task 4 correctly implements the multi-trigger validation layer: input validation is complete and consistent, on_start uniqueness is enforced at both the service pre-check and DB index levels (race-proof), projectId scoping is fail-closed throughout, DoS bounding covers both the trigger array cap and per-trigger keyword caps, no mass-assignment vector is open in the apply path, no PII/secrets appear in any new error message or log, and all 422 paths return machine-readable business codes without leaking internal state. Three low-severity observations are documented; none require blocking remediation.

findings.title: Error message embeds the normalized triggerType string (user-supplied, allowlisted)
findings.description: The message '"entryStepId is only allowed for the event trigger type (got " + type + ")"' echoes the `type` variable into the 422 response body. The value is the OUTPUT of normalizeTriggerType(), which has already validated and restricted it to the five-element VALID_TRIGGER_TYPES set (on_start|keyword|tag_added|custom_field_set|event). Because `type` can never carry arbitrary user input past that allowlist, this is NOT a reflection/injection risk. However, the pattern is a minor information-disclosure deviation from the project's PII-free error-message convention (the rest of the validate* methods never echo user-supplied values). The same pre-existing pattern also appears in invalidTriggerType() at line 902 ("Unknown trigger type: " + triggerType), which was introduced in prior phases.
findings.impact: Zero injection risk (allowlisted). The echoed value gives an attacker no more information than the business code alone. Very slight deviation from the project's no-user-value-in-messages style.
findings.recommendation: Optional: remove the '(got <type>)' suffix from the requireNoEntryStep message and use the business code alone for machine-readable feedback — consistent with how every other validator works (CODE_INVALID_ENTRY_STEP is already sufficient for the client to display a localized message). Not required for this phase; acceptable as-is given the allowlist guard.
findings.owasp: A04:2021 — Insecure Design (information disclosure, no exploitable attack)

findings.title: `MethodArgumentNotValidException` (400) path for @Size(max=50) on triggers array leaks field path
findings.description: When the triggers array or per-trigger keyword list exceeds the @Size cap at the bean-validation layer (before the request reaches FunnelService), Spring's MethodArgumentNotValidException fires. GlobalErrorHandler maps it to a 400 with a message like "triggers: size must be between 0 and 50" — this discloses the field path and cap limit, which differs from the 422+business-code contract the service layer enforces. The service re-checks the same cap (MAX_TRIGGERS=50) and returns a clean 422 `funnel_trigger_limit_reached`; the 400 path only fires if the controller binding validator runs first. This is a pre-existing pattern in the project (all DTO @Size annotations produce 400 via the same handler); Task 4 adds no new exposure beyond what existed, but callers may observe a different status code (400 vs 422) depending on which layer fires first.
findings.impact: Minimal. The 400 message reveals field names and cap values, which the API contract already documents. No PII, no cross-tenant data.
findings.recommendation: Low priority. If uniform 422+business-code is desired for the triggers cap, move the @Size check into a custom validator or rely solely on the service re-check (remove @Size from UpdateFunnelRequest and TriggerDto). Pre-existing pattern; not introduced by Task 4.
findings.owasp: A04:2021 — Insecure Design (contract inconsistency, not an exploitable vulnerability)

findings.category: A07 — Identification and Authentication Failures / Defense-in-depth observation
findings.title: checkTriggerConflict skip-on-null relies on caller discipline; no null-guard on the repo method Javadoc warning
findings.description: checkTriggerConflict correctly guards against passing null to the repo method: if onStartValue == null, it returns early (line 379-381). The FunnelRepository Javadoc explicitly documents that callers MUST NOT pass null. The risk is that a future caller or refactor of syncOnStartTriggerValue could break the invariant — for example, if bareOnStartTrigger() were changed to set triggerValue=null instead of "", syncOnStartTriggerValue would produce null, and the null guard in checkTriggerConflict would short-circuit the conflict check rather than error, silently allowing a duplicate. Currently the invariant holds: bareOnStartTrigger() sets triggerValue="", and syncOnStartTriggerValue maps blank→null correctly. No bug exists today.
findings.impact: No current exploitability. Risk is to future correctness if the null-vs-empty semantic of bareOnStartTrigger is changed without updating syncOnStartTriggerValue.
findings.recommendation: Low priority / forward-looking. Consider adding an assertion in syncOnStartTriggerValue (or a test) that verifies bare-start maps to null and never to empty string, to catch a regression early. The Javadoc warning on the repo method is good; a unit test asserting the null-means-skip behavior would close the loop.
findings.owasp: A07:2021 — Identification and Authentication Failures (future authentication bypass potential if invariant breaks)

verified_secure.area: Input validation — slug regex on triggerValue
verified_secure.detail: on_start: TRIGGER_VALUE_PATTERN ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,64}$ enforced by normalizeOnStartValue. event: EVENT_NAME_PATTERN ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$ enforced by requireEventSlugValue (1-char minimum, no empty slug). tag_added: TAG_SLUG_PATTERN ^[a-z0-9_-]{1,32}$ enforced by requireTagSlugValue. custom_field_set: non-blank enforced by requireFieldKeyValue. No bypass path found.

entryStepId for non-event types: strict reject via requireNoEntryStep (null check, 422). entryStepId for event type: requireEventEntryStep enforces non-null AND containment in the funnel's own step-id set. The step-id set is built from the full-replace steps array processed BEFORE applyTriggers, not from the stale persisted array — correct ordering in update(). entryStepId is NOT in validateSteps' generic edge-pass (carve-out correctly applied, mirrors SUBSCRIBE_TO_FUNNEL precedent).

MAX_KEYWORDS=50 and MAX_KEYWORD_LENGTH=64 enforced per-trigger by requireKeywords (for keyword type) and requireNoKeywords (for all others). Per-trigger @Size(max=50) annotation on TriggerDto.keywords provides an additional DTO-layer guard. normalizeKeywords lowercases, trims, drops blanks, and de-dupes before counting, so padding attacks cannot sneak past the cap.

verified_secure.area: Input validation — trigger array DoS cap
verified_secure.detail: MAX_TRIGGERS=50 checked at service entry (line 677) before any per-element processing. @Size(max=50) on UpdateFunnelRequest.triggers provides an upstream bean-validation guard. The default normalization (null/empty → single on_start) is safe and prevents a zero-trigger funnel.

verified_secure.area: on_start uniqueness — intra-funnel (at most one on_start element)
verified_secure.detail: onStartCount counter in applyTriggers increments for each on_start element and throws CODE_MULTIPLE_ON_START on the second occurrence. This check happens during the per-element loop before any DB access.

verified_secure.area: on_start uniqueness — cross-project (cannot be bypassed, race-proof)
verified_secure.detail: Service pre-check in checkTriggerConflict keys on onStartTriggerValue scalar scoped by projectId AND excludes self (id != conflict.id). The partial-unique DB index {projectId, onStartTriggerValue} filtered {status:active, onStartTriggerValue:{$exists:true}} is the second, race-closing line. DuplicateKeyException from the index is caught and mapped to 422 CODE_TRIGGER_CONFLICT (never 500). Bare /start ('') maps to null onStartTriggerValue → stays out of the index and the pre-check → no collision with other bare-start funnels. Cross-project isolation: all queries include projectId as the first field; funnelRepository.findByProjectIdAndOnStartTriggerValueAndStatus passes projectId explicitly.

verified_secure.area: projectId fail-closed scoping on conflict lookups (IDOR)
verified_secure.detail: requireFunnel() calls projectService.requireOwned() first, then filters funnelRepository.findById() by projectId — a cross-project funnelId returns the same uniform 404. checkTriggerConflict scopes the conflict lookup by funnel.getProjectId() (the funnel's owner projectId, not a caller-supplied one — cannot be forged). resolveSubscribeTarget() similarly filters by projectId. No cross-tenant data can be accessed via any new path in Task 4.

UpdateFunnelRequest carries @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true) — hostile fields (status, id, projectId) in the JSON body are silently dropped. TriggerDto also carries @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true). applyTriggers builds fresh Trigger domain objects field-by-field from validated DTO values; it never calls setTriggers() with a raw deserialized list. No path allows the caller to set funnel.status, funnel.projectId, or funnel.id through the PATCH body.

verified_secure.area: PII / secrets in error messages and logs
verified_secure.detail: All new 422 messages are static strings or contain only allowlisted type identifiers and integer caps — never user-supplied triggerValue, entryStepId, event name, keyword content, or subscriber data. The only log.warn() in FunnelService (line 1253) logs block type and character count — no user content. No new log statements were introduced in the Task 4 diff. The invalidTriggerType helper echoes the triggerType string, but this pre-existed Phase 3 and operates on an allowlisted value.

verified_secure.area: duplicate() reset — no inherited conflict payload
verified_secure.detail: duplicate() unconditionally sets a bareOnStartTrigger() (triggerValue='', entryStepId=null) and calls syncOnStartTriggerValue() which maps ''→null. The clone never inherits the original's on_start payload or event triggers. Draft funnels are excluded from the partial-unique index ($exists filter only matches non-null values), so a plain funnelRepository.save() on the clone cannot collide.

syncOnStartTriggerValue is the ONLY method that writes funnel.onStartTriggerValue. It is called from: create() (via the triggers init path), applyTriggers() end (covers all update paths), activate() (re-syncs before conflict check), and duplicate() (sets null). No code path sets onStartTriggerValue directly outside this helper.

Every public FunnelService method calls requireFunnel() which calls projectService.requireOwned() before any action. Cross-project funnel access collapses to uniform 404. Conflict lookups are projectId-scoped. No new endpoint or bypass path introduced by Task 4.

All trigger field values are strictly validated against allowlists and slug regexes before reaching the DB. FunnelRepository uses Spring Data derived queries (no raw MongoDB query construction from user strings) except the @Query on findByProjectIdAndTriggersTriggerTypeAndTriggersTriggerValue... which uses positional parameters (?0, ?1, ?2) — not string interpolation. No new raw string queries introduced in Task 4.

Trigger array cap (50 elements) + per-trigger keyword cap (50 keywords × 64 chars max) bound the PATCH payload and the DB document size. The service re-check fires before any per-element processing, preventing CPU exhaustion from a large array. See F1-F3 for minor observations; no exploitable DoS vector found.

All new tests in FunnelControllerIT and FunnelServiceTriggerTypeTest execute under @WithMockAppUser, and mutating endpoints use .with(csrf()). Authentication is inherited from the pre-existing test and service infrastructure.
